# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI agents and maintainers working in this repository.

## Project overview

This is the **asynchronous** VRChat API Python SDK (`vrchatapi` package). It is
generated from the [VRChat OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/vrchatapi/specification)
using the OpenAPI Generator `python` generator with `library=asyncio` and
`compatibleWithPythonLegacy=true`. All API methods are `async def` coroutines
backed by aiohttp.

### Golden rule

**Never hand-edit generated files.** `vrchatapi/**` and `docs/**` are disposable
outputs that are wiped and regenerated by `generate.sh`. All SDK behavior
changes must be implemented as:

- `generate.sh` changes (generator flags, post-processing steps), or
- patch files under `patches/` (applied by `generate.sh`), or
- the model post-processor `tools/make_models_lenient.py`, or
- hand-maintained files that are excluded from regeneration (see below).

If you need to change generated code, change the pipeline that produces it, then
regenerate. Never commit a one-off edit inside `vrchatapi/`.

## Repository layout

`generate.sh` wipes and regenerates `vrchatapi/`, `docs/`, and the packaging
files below; nothing in that set may be hand-edited. The generator's *default*
output also includes `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `pyproject.toml`, `.travis.yml`,
`test/`, and `.github/workflows/python.yml`; those are suppressed by
`.openapi-generator-ignore` so the repo can ship hand-maintained versions
instead (verified against a clean run with generator 7.24.0).

Generated (disposable, regenerated each run — never edit directly):

- `vrchatapi/` — the SDK package (models, api classes, api_client, rest, configuration, exceptions).
- `docs/` — per-model / per-API markdown reference.
- `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `requirements.txt`, `test-requirements.txt`, `tox.ini`,
  `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.openapi-generator/` (`FILES`, `VERSION`).

Hand-maintained — the generator never emits these:

- `generate.sh` — the single source of truth for building the SDK.
- `patches/` — behavior patches applied after generation.
- `tools/make_models_lenient.py` — model post-processor.
- `examples/`, `AGENTS.md`, `LICENSE` — documentation, kept async.
- `tests/`, `pytest.ini` — hand-written test suite. It lives in `tests/` (plural)
  so it never collides with the generator's `test/` (singular, ignored).
- `openapitools.json` — pinned generator version. The generator only creates it
  if absent, so our version survives regeneration.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — the only CI workflow.

Hand-maintained *because* `.openapi-generator-ignore` suppresses the
generator's default output:

- `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `pyproject.toml` — the hand-written versions win.
- `.travis.yml`, `.github/workflows/python.yml`, `git_push.sh` — deliberately
  not shipped (CI lives in `ci.yaml`; `git_push.sh` is a generator leftover —
  git is managed manually and by CI here).
- `.openapi-generator-ignore` itself — created by the generator only if missing;
  afterwards it is ours (entries are re-added by `generate.sh` each run).

Local artifacts that must never be committed: `*.egg-info/`, `__pycache__/`,
`.pytest_cache/`, `*.orig`, `*.rej`.

## Regenerating the SDK

Requirements on PATH:

- `openapi-generator` CLI — version pinned in `openapitools.json` (`7.24.0`);
  the `@openapitools/openapi-generator-cli` npm package is a convenient way to
  install it and reads `openapitools.json` automatically. Needs **Java 11+**.
- `git` and `redocly` — only needed when fetching the spec from GitHub.
- `yq` — only needed when `<version>` is omitted (the version is then read
  from the spec's `info.version`).

```bash
# Follow the latest specification (main branch), bundle it with redocly, regenerate:
bash generate.sh <version>          # e.g. 1.20.8

# Or use a pre-bundled single-file spec (deterministic, pinned):
bash generate.sh <version> /path/to/openapi-legacy.yaml

# Pristine baseline for patch work (stops before patches/ and model
# post-processing — see "How to add / update a patch" below):
bash generate.sh --no-patch <version> /path/to/openapi-legacy.yaml

# <version> may be omitted; it defaults to the spec's info.version (needs yq):
bash generate.sh /path/to/openapi-legacy.yaml
```

`generate.sh` does, in order: fetch+bundle the spec (or copy the given file) →
resolve `<version>` (explicit arg, or the spec's `info.version` via `yq`, with
`-nightly.` → `.dev` like the CI workflow) → `rm -rf vrchatapi docs` → generate
(`-g python --library=asyncio
--additional-properties=packageName=vrchatapi,projectName=vrchatapi-async,packageUrl=https://github.com/vrchatapi/vrchatapi-python,compatibleWithPythonLegacy=true`)
→ perl metadata fixes (stamps `VERSION` in `setup.py` and `__version__` in
`vrchatapi/__init__.py`, plus description, keywords, author, author_email,
`python_requires` (`>=3.10`), and `long_description` from `README.md` — all
metadata is declared in variables at
the top of `generate.sh`) → strip the API banner from sources → preserve
hand-maintained files via `.openapi-generator-ignore` → **with `--no-patch`,
stop here** → apply `patches/*.patch` → `tools/make_models_lenient.py` →
append `pytest-asyncio` to `test-requirements.txt`.

After regenerating, always run:

```bash
python -m compileall vrchatapi        # catch syntax issues (e.g. spec typos)
pytest                                # behavioral regression suite
```

Note: `pytest` starts a real local aiohttp server on `127.0.0.1`; in
sandboxed/containerized environments that bind localhost, run it with network
permission.

### Spec version policy

`generate.sh` follows the specification's `main` branch by default. To pin a
specific spec version, pass a bundled spec file. The repo's "legacy" bundle is
produced by `redocly bundle legacy-yaml` inside a clone of
`vrchatapi/specification` (the `legacy-yaml` API applies the `remove-x-internal`
decorator); this is what the previous synchronous SDK was generated from.

## Behavior patches (patches/)

These patches restore behavior of the original synchronous SDK that the stock
generator does not emit. Do not remove or weaken them without a strong reason.

| Patch | File | Preserves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rest_async.patch` | `rest.py` | Global `CookieJar` session cookies (VRChat login requires them), `_request_timeout` mapped to `aiohttp.ClientTimeout` (number and `(connect, read)` tuple), `trust_env=False` so proxies only come from `Configuration.proxy` like the sync SDK. |
| `2fa_verify_readable.patch` | `api_client.py` | 2FA / email-2FA response bodies raise `UnauthorizedException` with `status=200` and a readable `reason` ("2 Factor Authentication verification is required" / "Email ..."). |
| `safe_param_symbols.patch` | `configuration.py` | `safe_chars_for_path_param = '~()'` so path params keep `~()`. |
| `encode_basic_auth.patch` | `configuration.py` | Username/password are URL-encoded before base64 in `get_basic_auth_token()`. |
| `mime_type_fix.patch` | `models/mime_type.py` | The spec contains a full-width `＋` in `image/svg+xml`, which produces an invalid Python identifier; this patch renames it to `IMAGE_SLASH_SVG_XML` with the ASCII value. |

Boolean query parameters (`True`/`False` → `true`/`false`) are already handled
by the generator (`parameters_to_url_query`) — no patch needed. Non-2xx status
mapping (401/403/404/5xx → dedicated `ApiException` subclasses) is provided by
the generator's `ApiException.from_response`.

### How to add a patch

Generate the pristine baseline with `--no-patch`, then re-diff against it:

1. Generate the pristine baseline:
   `bash generate.sh --no-patch <version> [spec]`
   (stops right after the banner-strip / ignore-file step — exactly the state
   the `patch` steps in the full pipeline operate on).
2. Save the pristine baseline: `cp vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.pristine`.
3. Work on a copy: `cp vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.py` and edit
   `/tmp/<file>.py` (never edit inside `vrchatapi/`; it gets wiped).
4. Produce the unified diff with labels so `patch` applies cleanly:
   `diff -u -L a/vrchatapi/<file>.py -L b/vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.pristine /tmp/<file>.py > patches/<name>.patch`
5. Add a `patch ./vrchatapi/<file>.py < ./patches/<name>.patch` line to `generate.sh`.
6. Run the full pipeline and the test suite:
   `bash generate.sh <version> [spec] && python -m compileall vrchatapi && pytest`

### How to update an existing patch

When the spec or generator version changed, the old patch may no longer apply.
The `--no-patch` baseline is the safe way to rewrite it (no reverse-apply
trick needed):

1. Generate the pristine baseline: `bash generate.sh --no-patch <version> [spec]`.
2. Save the pristine baseline, then work on a copy:
   `cp vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.pristine`
   `cp vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.py` and edit `/tmp/<file>.py`.
3. (Optional) Check whether the old patch still fits the new output:
   `patch --dry-run ./vrchatapi/<file>.py < ./patches/<name>.patch`
   A clean dry run means only small tweaks are needed; `*.rej` means the hunks
   drifted and should be redone against the pristine file.
4. Regenerate the diff, overwriting the old patch:
   `diff -u -L a/vrchatapi/<file>.py -L b/vrchatapi/<file>.py /tmp/<file>.pristine /tmp/<file>.py > patches/<name>.patch`
5. Run the full pipeline and the test suite:
   `bash generate.sh <version> [spec] && python -m compileall vrchatapi && pytest`

`patch` may create `*.orig` backups when hunks apply at an offset and `*.rej`
when they fail; `generate.sh` deletes `*.orig` automatically — never commit
`*.orig`/`*.rej`.

## tools/make_models_lenient.py

The spec marks fields as `required` that the live API actually returns as `null`
(e.g. `CurrentUser.currentAvatar` for fresh accounts). Pydantic models reject
such payloads, which would break deserialization of real responses. This
post-processor rewrites every generated model so all fields are
`Optional[...]` with `default=None` — matching python-legacy's "all fields
default to None" semantics. It runs automatically in `generate.sh` and is
idempotent. If a future spec change fixes the nullability, this step can be
relaxed, but verify against real captured responses first.

## Behavioral contract (do not regress)

These behaviors are load-bearing for users; the test suite asserts them:

- Login flow: `GET /auth/user` sends URL-encoded basic auth, and the `auth`
  cookie set by the response is persisted and sent on subsequent requests.
- 2FA required responses raise a readable `UnauthorizedException`.
- Error mapping: 401 → `UnauthorizedException`, 403 → `ForbiddenException`,
  404 → `NotFoundException`, 5xx → `ServiceException` (plus generator-provided
  400/409/422 subclasses, all `ApiException` subclasses).
- Request bodies omit unset (`None`) fields; responses tolerate null/missing
  fields.
- Path params are encoded with the safe charset `~()`; boolean query params
  serialize as lowercase `true`/`false`.

## Async API deltas (intentional)

The SDK is intentionally async-only; do not reintroduce sync APIs:

- Methods are `async def` and must be awaited.
- `ApiClient` is used via `async with`.
- `async_req` and thread-pool async were removed.
- `foo_with_http_info()` returns an `ApiResponse` (`status_code`, `headers`,
  `data`, `raw_data`), not a `(data, status, headers)` tuple.
- `_preload_content` was removed; use `foo_without_preload_content()` to get the
  raw aiohttp response for streaming.
- Models are pydantic-backed with legacy-compatible `to_dict()`, `openapi_types`,
  and `attribute_map`.

## Testing

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt -r test-requirements.txt
pip install -e .
pytest
```

`tests/test_async_sdk.py` uses a real local aiohttp server and asserts the
behavioral contract above (cookies, 2FA, status mapping, serialization,
timeouts, streaming, context manager). Add a test for any behavior change.

## Publishing (OIDC)

Releases publish to PyPI with **trusted publishing (OIDC)** — no API token is
stored. The `publish` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` requests
`id-token: write` and is scoped to the `pypi` GitHub environment;
`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` exchanges the OIDC token automatically (no
`password` input).

Before publishing, the `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action` step
**auto-commits the freshly regenerated tree to `main`** with a
"Upgrade Python SDK to spec <version>" message, using `GITHUB_TOKEN` (needs
`contents: write`; no PAT). Despite the action's name this is **not** serving a
GitHub Pages site — it is the full-auto mechanism that keeps `main` in sync
with the latest spec on every release, so no Pages settings are needed.
Caveats:

- The push goes straight to `main`; if `main` later gets branch protection that
  requires pull requests, this step will fail.
- It commits whatever ref the `generate` job checked out, so for a clean
  full-auto release, trigger from `main` (the default for `workflow_dispatch`).

The `publish` job runs only on `repository_dispatch` or manual
`workflow_dispatch` (not on push/PR), and **any branch may trigger it** — the
release gate is human approval, not a branch check. On `workflow_dispatch` the
`release` input selects the mode:

- `none` (default) — CI only (generate/test/build/install), skip publish.
- `latest` — publish the latest spec version (read from the spec's
  `info.version`), no version typing needed.
- `prerelease` — publish `info.version` + `version_postfix` (e.g. `rc1` →
  `1.20.8rc1`), which PyPI treats as a prerelease; `version_postfix` is
  required in this mode.

Human approval is configured on the `pypi` GitHub environment, **not** in the
workflow YAML: Settings → Environments → `pypi` → Required reviewers. Until a
reviewer approves, the job is paused after the preceding generate/test/build/
install jobs finish. A GitHub environment does *not* restrict which branch can
publish — PyPI's trusted publisher validates owner/repo/workflow (and, if
registered, the environment name) but never the ref; restrict branches in the
workflow `if` if that is ever wanted.

PyPI-side setup (one time): register a **pending publisher** for the
`vrchatapi-async` project with this repository's owner/name, workflow
`ci.yaml`, and environment `pypi` (must match the job's `environment:`).

## Common maintenance tasks

- **Bump the spec / regenerate:** `bash generate.sh <version>` and commit the
  regenerated output together with any patch updates.
- **Add a behavior fix:** prefer a patch under `patches/` (see workflow above).
- **Upgrade openapi-generator:** edit `openapitools.json`, then verify the gate:
  `openapi-generator config-help -g python` must list `compatibleWithPythonLegacy`
  and `library` must include `asyncio`. Re-run `generate.sh` and the test suite.
- **Update docs/examples:** edit `README.md` / `examples/` directly (they are
  excluded from regeneration); keep all examples async.
